summary: Accounting journal domain foundation in flat accounting microservice layout.

findings: Accounting journal domain foundation stays pure-domain with explicit typed inputs/outputs instead of runtime special cases.
journal posting validates legal_entity_id, open period, source documents, approval evidence, and balanced debit/credit totals
oya-accounting-journal-domain lives under a flat microservice path, preserving independent release/scale ownership.
The slice avoids production compliance/SLO claims and models source-versioned evidence refs only.

F3_adversarial.diagnostic_asserted: Negative tests reject missing required evidence, malformed refs/digests, unbalanced totals, single-line self-balancing debit+credit entries, missing payroll digest/wage refs, and invalid close states before accepting domain results.
findings: cargo test -p oya-accounting-journal-domain passes 5 integration tests.
Public API is constrained to domain constructors/evaluators in oya-accounting-journal-domain.
README/PRD entrypoints point to canonical machine-readable spec and clarify non-ownership.
Verification passed: cargo fmt, cargo test -p oya-accounting-journal-domain, cargo clippy -p oya-accounting-journal-domain --all-targets -- -D warnings.
cargo-prefix, slo-coverage, cargo deny, cargo tree, and JSON parse evidence are recorded in verification.

alternatives_named: implement runtime adapters and filing transports now
land flat microservice domain foundation first
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: Flat microservice domain foundation is the smallest architecture-compliant slice that creates testable invariants without false production claims.
rejected_reasons: Enterprise-suite crate names conflict with ADR-0131/ADR-0132 forward policy.
Runtime adapters/filing transports need separate secrets, ops, workflow, and regulator evidence gates.

findings: Tenant/legal-entity ids are required before accepted domain outputs are produced.
Refs/digests are metadata-only and validation rejects prefix-only/traversal/secret-shaped inputs.

F8_performance.regression_baseline: No prior native domain crate existed; no hot-path runtime claim is made.

findings.summary: Pure in-memory validation over bounded input vectors; no database/network/async hot path introduced.

findings: The implementation treats payroll/accounting rules as rulepack/evidence refs and does not encode tax rates or claim statutory filing certification.
All public struct fields in the new crate carry data_class comments.

Additive workspace member and microservice folder; rollback removes microservices/accounting/crates/oya-accounting-journal-domain, catalog rows, and spec/test-ref alignment. No migration or persisted data exists.
No runtime telemetry introduced in domain-only crate; future app/rest/worker slices must emit audit-chain/OTel events before production claims.
Machine-readable spec crate refs/test refs were aligned from earlier oya-enterprise-* names to flat oya-<ms>-<bc>-<layer> names. No external API compatibility exists yet.

M1_challenge_assumption.premise_stated: Implementing enterprise foundations ahead of cloud integration is useful only if each service stays flat and domain-only until runtime evidence exists.
M1_challenge_assumption.premise_evidence_ref: ADR-0131/ADR-0132 + specs/microservices/*.json + official source URLs in tasks/enterprise-microservices-plan.md
M1_challenge_assumption.do_nothing_consequence: Payroll/accounting would remain planned-only, blocking later enterprise cloud integration seams.
M1_challenge_assumption.upstream_fix_rejection_reason: Waiting for all cloud/runtime integrations would delay testable domain invariants; domain crates are reversible and evidence-bounded.

findings: Fits ADR-0315 compositional ERP doctrine: HR, Payroll, and Accounting remain separate services connected by typed refs/events.
Package name oya-accounting-journal-domain follows oya-<ms>-<bc>-<layer>.
README and PRD transition documents clarify canonical machine-readable spec authority.
Implementation resides under microservices/accounting/crates/oya-accounting-journal-domain with per-service catalog and central aggregation row.
No storage/network/workflow execution/regulator filing/cloud adapter introduced.
The package depends only on oya-data-boundary-kernel.
Accounting AC-01..AC-05 acceptance refs point to existing flat accounting crate tests.
Validation is deterministic and rejects incomplete state instead of estimating regulated calculations.

verification.notes: duplicate cpufeatures and pre-existing cloud IAM/KMS wildcard path warnings

verification.command: python3 JSON parse evidence + audit-chain JSONL

remaining_risks: No REST/API/runtime/storage/workflow dispatch/statutory filing/SLO evidence claimed.
Full oya verify --ci-required not claimed because broad repo has known pre-existing catalog/data-class blockers.
